prerequisites: No prerequisites. Recommended are the competencies taught in the basic modules of Computer Science and the advanced modules Software Engineering and Software Internship.

learning_outcomes.text: explain the differences between textual and visual languages
describe methods for defining visual languages
use basic designer tools for visual languages
familiarize themselves with an unknown visual language and evaluate it using a small test application
apply scientific working methods in independently identifying, formulating, and solving problems
speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion

syllabus_topics: Modeling languages (e.g., Unified Modeling Language (UML), SDL, Petri nets, Statecharts)
Visual development environments (e.g., Eclipse, AndroidStudio) components for visual management of software projects
Visual implementation of graphical user interfaces
Discussion of advantages and disadvantages of visual concepts
Possibilities and limitations of visual languages in the software development process

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercise assignments (at least 50% of points)
Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercise assignments
Oral examination (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: Assessment is based on achieving at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and an oral presentation of the solution to at least two exercise assignments. The examination performance is an oral examination or a written exam. Grading is from 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
